title: Your first Java program
summary: What every line of Main.java does, then run it.

say.never: In this guide you will open Main.java and look at each line to see what it does. Then you will run it and check that it prints what you expect.
say.bit: In this guide you will open Main.java, see what each line does, then run it.

say.never: Every Java program starts somewhere. Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Main`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Every Java program starts somewhere. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Main` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: It may be further down. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `public class Main` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `public class Main` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find public class Main with Ctrl+F.

say.never: `public class Main` is a **class**, which is just a container that holds your code. Think of it as the folder tab for this program. The file has the same name, `Main.java`. All your code lives between the opening curly brace `{` and the very last closing one `}`.
say.bit: `public class Main` is the **class**: a container for code. The file's name matches it (`Main.java`). Everything else goes between its `{` and the last `}`.

say.never: It may be further down. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `public static void main` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `public static void main` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find public static void main with Ctrl+F.

say.never: `main` is the spot where Java starts reading your program. Every program needs this exact line. For now, **copy it exactly** and don't worry about what each word means. You'll learn them later, one at a time.
say.bit: `main` is the method Java runs first. Copy this line exactly in every program for now; you'll learn what each word means in the Methods lesson.

say.never: It may be further down. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `System.out.println` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `System.out.println` and press Enter to jump to it.

say.never: `System.out.println(...)` tells the computer to **print** a line of text on the screen. Whatever is inside the double quotes is printed exactly as you typed it. That text in quotes is called a **String**. Every Java statement ends with a `;`, like the full stop at the end of a sentence, and this line is missing its `;`. And see the `//` at the start of the line? That makes it a **comment**: a note for people that Java skips. Right now this line does nothing.
say.bit: `System.out.println(...)` prints a line of text. The text in double quotes is a **String**, printed exactly as written. Every statement ends with a `;`, and this one is missing it. The `//` in front makes it a **comment**, so Java skips it for now.

say.never: Three small fixes to this one line. First, click right after the `//` at the start of the `System.out.println` line and press **Backspace** twice to delete both slashes. Now the line is real code, and a red wavy line shows up: that's the editor telling you something is missing. Second, change `YOUR NAME` to your own name, keeping the quote marks around it. Third, click at the very end of the line, after the `)`, and type `;`. The red line goes away. Save with **Ctrl+S**.
say.bit: Delete the `//` in front of `System.out.println`, change `YOUR NAME` to your name (keep the quotes), add a `;` at the end after the `)`, and save with **Ctrl+S**.

hint.never: delete the //, type your name, and add the ;.
hint.bit: uncomment it, add your name and the ;.

say.never: Click the **Run** button, the little triangle (▷) Dozer is pointing at, up at the top right of the file. Your program runs, and whatever it prints shows up in the **terminal** at the bottom of the screen. You should see your own name!
say.bit: Click the **Run** button (▷) Dozer is pointing at. Your greeting appears in the terminal at the bottom.
